document.title: Sophia AI Real-Time Architecture and Future Build Standard
scope: AI, voice, avatar and research providers
mandatory architecture rules for future development

interpretation.currentState: Facts observed in the repositories at the recorded snapshots.
interpretation.targetState: The required design for all new work and the direction for refactoring existing code.
interpretation.priority: The target-state rules are architectural requirements, not a claim that the current implementation already satisfies them.

architectureSummary.style: Browser real-time client plus a dedicated session runtime and a separate business-system API.
primaryComponents: Express 5 Business Manager API on Node.js 20
provider adapters for real-time AI and avatars
architectureSummary.centralRule: Business behavior, tools, prompts, bookings and domain knowledge must remain independent of any AI, voice, avatar, search or transport provider.

providerPolicy.requiredPattern: Ports and adapters with dependency-injected provider registries and capability-based resolution.
providerPolicy.configurationSource: Server-side customer and experience configuration, with environment variables or a secret manager holding credentials.
providerPolicy.clientResponsibility: The browser requests an experience and consumes a normalized session/transport contract; it must not decide the vendor composition.
providerPolicy.secretPolicy: Provider API keys and long-lived credentials never enter Angular or API responses.

targetFrontendBoundary.request: Send experienceId, customer/device identity and supported browser capabilities.
targetFrontendBoundary.response: Receive a normalized session descriptor with transport type, ephemeral credentials, media mode, UI capabilities and tool-delivery mode.
targetFrontendBoundary.implementation: A frontend TransportAdapterRegistry resolves adapters by protocol/capability. The page component must not branch on vendor names.
targetFrontendBoundary.allowedVendorCode: Only inside adapter implementations and their provider-specific tests.

endpoints.purpose: Validate, execute and record a runtime tool call
Close provider transports and persist the closed state

validation: NestJS ValidationPipe with whitelist, transform and forbidNonWhitelisted
Zod strict schemas for tool inputs

currentSessionSelection.tavusPath: Special branch in ConversationService when dto.aiProvider equals tavus-full.
currentSessionSelection.configuration: Environment variables plus client-provided provider fields.
currentSessionSelection.databaseConfigStatus: sophia_runtime.ai_configs exists and is seeded, but current session creation does not resolve it.

mandatoryTargetModel.principle: Provider names are configuration data, never domain logic.

ports.name: ConversationProvider
ports.responsibility: Create and close sessions and expose normalized events, messages and interruption controls.

ports.name: SpeechProvider
ports.responsibility: Optional transcription and speech synthesis capabilities when they are not part of a composite provider.

ports.name: AvatarProvider
ports.responsibility: Create avatar sessions and accept normalized text or audio input.

ports.name: ResearchProvider
ports.responsibility: Search only approved domains, return source metadata and enforce freshness policy.

ports.name: ToolTransport
ports.responsibility: Deliver provider tool calls to the runtime and return results exactly once.

ports.name: MediaTransport
ports.responsibility: Describe how the browser joins and renders audio/video without exposing vendor decisions to the page.

registryBehavior: NestJS multi-provider registration discovers adapters at startup.
A ProviderResolver selects adapters from an ExperienceProfile and required capabilities.
The resolver rejects unsupported combinations before creating external sessions.
Composite providers such as Tavus may satisfy multiple capability axes with one adapter.
Adding a provider must not require edits to ConversationService, domain tools or the kiosk component.

experienceProfile.identity: Stable internal experienceId such as essential, professional or premium.
experienceProfile.clientContract: Angular sends experienceId and never sends raw providerId in the public kiosk flow.

configurationRules: No switch statement over provider names in controllers, domain services or UI components.
No provider URL, model name, voice name, persona ID, replica ID or avatar ID in domain code.
No provider SDK import outside its adapter package.
No long-lived provider secret in PostgreSQL plaintext, Angular configuration, logs or API responses.
Environment variables or a secret manager provide credentials keyed by provider configuration.
Database configuration selects profiles and aliases; adapters translate aliases into vendor-specific values.

contract.execution: Async function with customerId, sessionId and storeId context
contract.persistence: Successful calls are written to sophia_runtime.tool_calls

domainIsolation.currentBehavior: Student tool calls clear pending property-review state; property tool calls clear pending student-consultation review state.
requiredBehavior: Classify each turn into one domain before exposing or selecting tools.
Expose the minimum tool set required for the active domain and task.
Never use property knowledge as a fallback for student migration or vice versa.
Domain routing must be deterministic application logic with model assistance, not prompt text alone.

requiredImprovements: Record pending, succeeded and failed tool calls, including provider call ID and real start/completion timestamps.
Persist review/confirmation state or issue signed short-lived review tokens; do not keep booking authorization only in process memory.
Apply tool timeouts, cancellation and per-tool retry policy.
Version tool schemas so providers can synchronize changes before user sessions.
Pre-provision Tavus or other remote tools during deployment rather than the first customer session.

supportedJourneys: review customer, email, property and time
generate sale property report and send it with confirmation
realEstate.sourceOfTruth: Business Manager PostgreSQL tables and services
realEstate.mutationRule: reviewInspectionBooking must precede bookInspection and the confirmed payload must match the reviewed payload.
realEstate.saleDelivery: Sale bookings enqueue a property-report job; the confirmation delivery waits for the report or follows the configured fallback path.
realEstate.rentalDelivery: Rental bookings queue or send the confirmation without a property report.

supportedJourneys: verify current rules against official sources
show effects for new and existing students
review name, email, time and optional enquiry summary
studentAgency.sourceOfTruth: Approved Business Manager knowledge rows plus retrieved official-source snapshots
studentAgency.officialSourcePolicy: Use official Australian Government sources first. If official verification fails, clearly report that it could not be verified and offer adviser review; do not invent an answer.
studentAgency.mutationRule: reviewStudentConsultation must precede bookStudentConsultation and the confirmed payload must match the reviewed payload.
studentAgency.demoRule: Demo consultation slots must be described as demonstrations and must not imply a real adviser meeting.

requiredSteps: Ask the customer to check the details, especially email spelling.
Wait for an explicit confirmation in a subsequent user turn.
Reject booking if displayed data changed or confirmation is absent.
Use an idempotency key for the mutation.
Report queued, sent, failed and pending-report states accurately.
confirmationStandard.futureRequirement: Confirmation state must be enforced server-side and survive restarts and horizontal scaling.

tables.ai_configs: Intended customer/device provider configuration; currently not used by session resolution
tables.sessions: Normalized runtime and provider session lifecycle
tables.tool_calls: Tool request and output audit records
tables.events: Reserved event audit table; current application writes are not established

logicalOwnership.migrationMechanism: Ordered SQL migrations run with npm run migrate

logicalOwnership.schema: public and existing Business Manager tables
logicalOwnership.otherData: Business Manager, users, AI Toolkit, Town Planner and payment tables remain outside the Sophia real-time domain.
logicalOwnership.migrationMechanism: SQL scripts plus startup schema guards in the Express service

crossServiceRules: The runtime accesses business data only through authenticated Business Manager APIs, not by importing Business Manager models.
Do not create foreign keys across independently deployable database ownership boundaries.
Store timestamps as timestamptz and return authoritative timezone labels from the business service.
Use JSONB for provider metadata only when fields are provider-specific or intentionally extensible; promote query-critical fields to typed columns.

targetConfigurationTables.name: experience_profiles
targetConfigurationTables.purpose: Provider-neutral customer/plan composition and enabled capabilities

targetConfigurationTables.name: provider_configurations
targetConfigurationTables.purpose: Non-secret provider settings, adapter version and credential reference

targetConfigurationTables.name: session_capabilities
targetConfigurationTables.purpose: Resolved immutable capability snapshot for each session

targetConfigurationTables.name: booking_reviews
targetConfigurationTables.purpose: Durable review payload hash, expiry and confirmation status

requiredImprovements: Use explicit scopes for student-agency and real-estate access instead of the current real-estate-only scope label.
Add request correlation IDs propagated from browser to runtime, Business Manager and workers.
Use typed/generated API contracts or a shared schema package without sharing persistence models.
Define retry behavior only for safe reads and idempotent writes.

queueStandard: Persist status, attempt count, next attempt, lease owner, lease expiry, sent time and last error.
Workers claim atomically and recover expired leases.
API success means accepted/queued unless provider delivery is synchronously confirmed.
Never use the AI Toolkit daily cron for booking confirmations.
Expose delivery state to operations and support safe manual retry.

currentControls: Provider API keys remain in backend environment configuration.
OpenAI uses short-lived Realtime client secrets.
Tavus conversations require auth and return meeting tokens.
Business Manager integration uses a constant-time bearer-token comparison.
HTTP DTOs and tool inputs are validated.
Database access uses parameterized queries for runtime values.
mandatoryRules: Authenticate and authorize session creation; never trust plan or provider selection from the browser.
Bind sessionId to customerId, deviceId and experienceId.
Rate-limit session creation and tool execution by tenant and device.
Redact provider tokens, email addresses and conversation content from routine logs.
Encrypt secret references and personal data according to retention policy.
Use least-privilege service credentials and rotate them.
Validate provider webhook/app-message identity and deduplicate provider call IDs.
Apply an allowlist of official domains for regulated student-information research.

requiredIdentifiers: provider session ID in protected logs
requiredMetrics: session creation latency by stage and provider
email/report queue age, retries and failures
provider minutes, tokens and cost by tenant/experience
currentGaps: tool timing begins at database insertion after execution, so it cannot measure true tool latency
events table is not consistently populated
provider setup and conversation creation are combined in the Premium startup path
no normalized per-provider usage ledger is present

sessionStartup: Warm and health-check providers before customer interaction.
Synchronize remote tool schemas during deployment or a controlled background task.
Run independent session and media setup concurrently only when lifecycle cleanup is deterministic.
Record stage timings separately: runtime, provider, transport join, microphone, remote media and first response.
turnHandling: Select one domain and the minimum tool set per turn.
Avoid model-generated filler that can create duplicate speech or hide failures.
Stream speech when the provider supports it.
Cache only source content with explicit freshness and jurisdiction metadata.
Do not add UI loading messages that trigger extra model or network calls.
resilience: Every external call has a timeout.
Cancellation closes partially created provider sessions.
Fallbacks must preserve the requested domain and must never silently substitute unverified information.
Circuit breakers and provider health must influence provider resolution where a configured fallback exists.

targetSessionFlow: Angular requests POST /sessions with experienceId and device context.
Runtime authenticates the caller and loads the customer-owned ExperienceProfile.
Provider registries resolve adapters for the plan without vendor branching in ConversationService.
Runtime creates provider sessions, records the resolved capability snapshot and returns a normalized TransportDescriptor.
Angular TransportAdapterRegistry connects the required media transports.
DomainRouter selects a domain and enables only the relevant tool group.
All tool calls enter the same server-side ToolExecutionPipeline for validation, authorization, idempotency, audit and output normalization.
Mutation tools require a durable reviewed payload and explicit confirmation token.
Session close is idempotent and closes every allocated provider resource.

sessionDescriptor.rule: Vendor payloads are translated inside adapters and do not leak into the domain contract.

toolResult.rule: Display data and spoken content are explicit fields; the frontend does not scrape markdown or infer domain from prose.

providerIndependence: Depend on interfaces and capability types, never concrete provider classes outside composition roots.
Keep provider SDK types inside adapters.
Use stable internal aliases for models and voices.
Write provider contract tests that every adapter must pass.
A new provider is complete only when it can be enabled through configuration without editing domain flows.
domainDesign: Keep real estate and student migration as separate bounded contexts.
Share orchestration primitives, not domain data or fallback answers.
Use explicit application services for search, review, confirm, book and delivery status.
Prompts guide conversational behavior; code and persisted state enforce authorization and workflow order.
apiAndData: Version public and provider callback contracts.
Use schema migrations for durable data changes; startup guards may verify but must not become the primary migration system.
All mutations require idempotency and an audit trail.
Do not return success before the database transaction commits.
Represent asynchronous delivery accurately as queued, processing, sent or failed.
testing: Unit-test domain services without provider SDKs.
Run one shared contract suite for every conversation, avatar, research and tool-transport adapter.
Integration-test Runtime to Business Manager against a disposable PostgreSQL database.
End-to-end test Essential, Professional and Premium for both business domains.
Include multilingual, interruption, duplicate-answer, tool-timeout and session-cleanup scenarios.
Use provider sandboxes or recorded contract fixtures in CI; reserve metered live smoke tests for releases.
releaseGates: Database migrations applied and backward-compatible for the deployment window.
Both domain booking flows pass through review, explicit confirmation and email queueing.
No provider secret appears in frontend artifacts or logs.
Startup and turn latency remain within the agreed service-level objectives.
Rollback commit or immutable previous deployment is identified before release.
Production smoke sessions are closed and test bookings are clearly labelled.

evidence: RuntimeConfig.aiProvider is typed and assigned only as openai-realtime.
ProvidersModule binds AI_PROVIDER directly to OpenAIRealtimeProvider.
Angular experienceConfiguration maps plans directly to vendor names.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: ExperienceProfile plus capability resolver and provider registries.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Booking review authorization is held in in-memory maps and frontend flags.
currentTechnicalDebt.impact: It is vulnerable to process restarts, horizontal scaling and event-order problems.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Durable review record or signed review token enforced by the server.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Premium provider tool synchronization runs during the first session of a process.
currentTechnicalDebt.impact: Cold starts can add substantial latency.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Deployment-time tool provisioning with version/hash checks.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: The runtime database ai_configs table is not used to resolve sessions.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Replace or evolve it into active ExperienceProfile configuration.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Provider entitlements can be requested from the browser.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Resolve allowed experiences server-side from authenticated tenant/plan data.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Tool failures are not recorded by ToolRegistryService.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Insert pending before execution and update succeeded/failed in a finally-safe pipeline.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: The Angular kiosk component owns substantial provider and domain orchestration.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Split session facade, transport registry, domain view stores and booking workflow services.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Demo device and store identifiers are hardcoded in Angular.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Provisioned device configuration or authenticated runtime bootstrap.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Express startup code applies schema guards in production.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: A single ordered migration pipeline with recorded migration versions.

currentTechnicalDebt.item: Runtime and Business Manager may share one Neon project even though they have separate ownership.
currentTechnicalDebt.target: Keep separate schemas at minimum and prefer separate database projects where operationally justified.

implementationRoadmap.name: Stabilize contracts and observability
deliverables: Introduce experienceId while maintaining temporary compatibility with current provider fields.
Define normalized SessionDescriptor, ToolResult and provider capability contracts.
Record pending, failed and succeeded tool calls with accurate timings.
Add correlation IDs and startup/turn metrics.
Persist booking-review authorization.

implementationRoadmap.name: Complete the backend provider abstraction
deliverables: Create ConversationProviderRegistry, ResearchProviderRegistry and capability resolver.
Adapt OpenAI Realtime and Tavus Full to the same session orchestration port.
Move all vendor branches out of ConversationService.
Resolve ExperienceProfiles from server-side configuration.
Add provider contract tests.

implementationRoadmap.name: Normalize browser transports
deliverables: Create TransportAdapterRegistry in Angular.
Move OpenAI, Daily/Tavus, LiveAvatar and Simli branches out of the kiosk component.
Split domain view state into student and real-estate stores.
Remove vendor IDs from public experience types.

implementationRoadmap.name: Operationalize providers and queues
deliverables: Provision remote provider tools during deployment.
Add provider readiness checks and configured fallback policies.
Add queue dashboards, alerts and manual retry controls.
Add provider usage and cost ledger.

implementationRoadmap.name: Enforce full release standards
deliverables: End-to-end matrix for every plan, language and business domain.
Latency budgets and regression alerts.
Automated secret scanning and frontend artifact checks.
Documented rollback and provider outage runbooks.

definitionOfDoneForNewProvider: Provider manifest declares capabilities and configuration schema.
Adapter implements the required port without changing domain services.
Credentials are server-side and returned credentials are short-lived.
Adapter passes the shared contract suite.
Session close and partial-start cleanup are idempotent.
Tool delivery is deduplicated and correlated.
Startup, turn, error and usage metrics are emitted.
The provider is enabled by an ExperienceProfile configuration change.
Angular uses an existing normalized transport adapter or adds one without changing the kiosk domain logic.
Both real-estate and student-agency tool suites pass where the provider claims tool support.
Multilingual speech and interruption are explicitly tested if advertised.
Operational and rollback instructions are documented.
